subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should true Microsoft Teams app-management removal use this non-destructive boundary: remove the cached Teams conversation reference and mark matching OpenClaw sessions stale without deleting retained transcript/session data?
rationale: The code path is a plausible plugin-owned fix, but the permanent retention behavior controls sensitive personal-chat history after app removal and should be accepted by a maintainer rather than inferred from tests.

options.title: Accept stale-session plus reference removal
options.body: Adopt the PR's non-destructive boundary, require after-fix live proof, and keep destructive transcript deletion out of runtime unless a separate retention policy is approved.

options.title: Narrow to session staling only
options.body: Keep the fix focused on preventing old context reuse, but explicitly leave proactive conversation-reference tombstoning for a separate decision.

options.title: Require destructive cleanup policy first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define whether Teams app removal must delete retained transcript or session data, which would need broader data-loss review.

recommendation.title: Accept stale-session plus reference removal
recommendation.body: Adopt the PR's non-destructive boundary, require after-fix live proof, and keep destructive transcript deletion out of runtime unless a separate retention policy is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Teams state-store migration and retention-adjacent work make this the best available owner for the removal-boundary policy choice.
